# Hawkinsonwb Skills

Use the installed skill that matches the requested phase. Read its `SKILL.md` and relevant bundled references before applying it. Follow the current project's workspace guidance and tracker conventions.

Planning establishes scope and acceptance criteria; implementation keeps the user involved in consequential decisions and shared contracts. A continuation request preserves existing authorization. Select a workflow from the user's intent rather than starting every phase automatically.

If skills are unavailable, report the installation gap and use the README's installation instructions. This routing context does not replace the full skill instructions.

## Available skills

- `code-review`: Review product requirements, architectural changes, and code correctness in a PR or change set, and produce concise evidence-backed findings, preferably inline.
- `follow-up`: Resume an established task after waiting or continue from current context; handle PR review feedback through the dedicated review guide.
- `noodle`: Clarify an idea through product planning stages or work out an implementation plan for an already defined outcome. Use before task creation or delivery when decisions still need discussion.
- `noodle-big`: Explore broad product features or whole projects through staged product discussion, milestones, and dependency-linked tasks. Use when the scope spans multiple user journeys or workstreams.
- `setup-hawkinsonwb-skills`: Set up workspace and repository agent guidance for the Hawkinsonwb Skills workflow, including repository boundaries, ticket tracking, validation, and review conventions. Use when adopting the skills across a project or workspace.
- `work`: Implement an agreed task with scaffolding first, user alignment on core logic, and acceptance validation. Use when the user is ready to deliver a planned change.

# Repository conventions

These maintenance conventions apply when editing the `hawkinsonwb/Skills` repository. When this collection is installed as a plugin in another project, use that project's guidance and the requested skill instead.

Keep the canonical skill collection in `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. Add each skill once; the installer and Claude plugin consume that directory directly.

When adding or editing skills, follow the Agent Skills specification linked in README.md. Keep shared instructions portable, declare tool requirements, and place supporting resources inside the skill folder with relative references.

Keep README installation instructions current when distribution changes. Update `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`'s version when releasing plugin changes so installed plugins can receive updates.

Keep examples in documentation rather than installable skill folders. Each skill must remain usable when installed individually, including its supporting resources.

Harness metadata, discovery rules, and `AGENTS.md` are generated. After changing skills, `docs/harness-context.md`, `docs/repository-conventions.md`, or Claude plugin metadata, run `python3 scripts/build-harness-files.py`; check with `python3 scripts/build-harness-files.py --check`. Maintain release metadata in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, routing wording in `docs/harness-context.md`, and these maintenance instructions in `docs/repository-conventions.md`.
